stem.text: When $\alpha$-particles are directed at gold leaf:

items: almost all $\alpha$-particles pass through without deflection
a few $\alpha$-particles are deviated through large angles.

stem.text: What are the reasons for these effects?

A.text: most $\alpha$-particles have enough energy to pass right through the gold leaf; gold is very dense so a few low energy $\alpha$-particles bounce back from the gold surface

B.text: most $\alpha$-particles miss all gold atoms; a few $\alpha$-particles bounce off gold atoms

C.text: the gold nucleus is very small so most $\alpha$-particles miss all nuclei; occasionally the path of an $\alpha$-particle is close to a nucleus

D.text: the positive charge in an atom is not concentrated enough to deflect an $\alpha$-particle; occasionally an $\alpha$-particle experiences many small deflections in the same direction
